evidence.note: Cargo init followed by a dependency-compile check — a foundational milestone with a done-check, showing dependency-aware sequencing before building on top.

Wrote transport/message-loop shell first, then incrementally verified tree-sitter parser API (probe language() -> LANGUAGE -> parser setup), each gated by cargo check. Demonstrates a workable transport->parser layer order with compile-level success criteria.

Single big-bang implementation of all handlers (folding, selection, symbols, highlights, definitions) at once, coupled with a golden lookup — no per-handler milestones, no prioritization by test weight.
Identified the 12 methods and examined response shapes/key-uniqueness, but this fed a memorization lookup rather than an ordered plan to convert effort into passing tests handler-by-handler.
Release build then a single full golden-suite run at the very end — no incremental per-layer functional exit criteria; verification was compilation until the final all-at-once test.

reasoning: The agent identified the major layers (transport, parser, handlers) and tackled them in a broadly correct dependency order with compile checks acting as rough per-step criteria, exceeding a merely vague mental list (anchor 3). However it lacks an explicit ordered milestone plan with concrete functional done-criteria, never did a 'first method end-to-end' incremental loop, ran the golden suite only once at the very end, and its reliance on a golden lookup table meant it never prioritized handlers by their weight in golden.jsonl. This falls short of the workable-layered anchor at 5 and well short of the explicit-milestone anchor at 8, landing at 4.
